claims.text: The precursor is an equiatomic Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr metallic/hydride powder blend containing 5 wt% Mg powder.
The specified metallic and hydride powder blend can be processed by ink-extrusion additive manufacturing.
TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2 decompose sequentially within the respective proposed windows of 450-600, 500-650, 600-750, 700-850, and 750-900°C.
Heating at 10°C/min with a one-hour dwell at each decomposition step will provide adequate dehydrogenation without premature alloying or incomplete decomposition.
Homogenization at 1100°C for two hours is sufficient to homogenize the HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Sequential hydride decomposition releases hydrogen and leaves metal atoms that alloy in situ.
Mg reacts with oxygen during processing to form MgO.
The Mg getter scavenges oxygen originating from hydride decomposition and atmospheric leaks.
A 5 wt% Mg addition combined with an oxygen partial pressure below 1 ppm reduces oxygen activity below the threshold for alpha-HCP formation.
Suppressing oxygen uptake prevents alpha-Ti or other alpha-HCP phases from nucleating.
Rapid water quenching from 1100°C suppresses diffusion-controlled phase separation.
Rapid quenching from 1100°C traps a metastable single-phase beta-BCC HfNbTaTiZr structure.
The rapidly quenched alloy will have a grain size of 1-5 micrometers.
The processed alloy will attain greater than 98% density.
Slow cooling produces a dual-phase alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC microstructure.
Slow cooling produces grains in the range of 5-20 micrometers.
Without Mg or adequate oxygen control, dissolved oxygen causes alpha-HCP phase formation.
Formation of oxygen-induced alpha-HCP phases degrades mechanical properties.
Detection of alpha-Ti diffraction peaks between 450 and 900°C would demonstrate insufficient oxygen scavenging by Mg.
Observation of a dual-phase structure or grains larger than 5 micrometers after rapid quenching would falsify the predicted quenched microstructure.

contradictions.description: The feed contains 5 wt% Mg and the hypothesis explicitly predicts formation of MgO, yet the final material is described without qualification as an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr single-phase beta-BCC alloy. No removal or exclusion pathway for Mg/MgO is specified; retained MgO would constitute an additional phase and alter the overall composition.
